title: The AI editor that can reject the brief
target_audience: AI-native operators building repeatable content systems

claims.text: The engine separates non-negotiable editorial gates from growth potential.

slides.headline: This AI editor is allowed to say no.

slides.question_answered: Why is producing the brief not enough?
slides.headline: A brief does not become good because it arrived.
slides.body: Content for content's sake is still pointless when a machine makes it faster.

slides.question_answered: How does the engine judge an idea?
slides.headline: The engine asks two different questions.
slides.body: First, can this be said? Then, is it worth saying?

slides.question_answered: What has to happen before rendering?
slides.headline: Rendering comes after the thinking.

slides.question_answered: Do the gates slow production down?
slides.headline: More gates add friction. Weak content burns more time.
slides.body: The useful automation is not the one that makes the most. It is the one that knows what deserves making.

slides.headline: The render is the last step, not the first.

editorial.strongest_reason_to_reject: The example is system-led, so it needs a concrete owned artifact to avoid reading as process theatre.
editorial.audience_payoff: Operators get a repeatable way to stop weak content before production cost compounds.
editorial.countercase: Extra gates can slow low-risk work, so the system keeps engagement warnings overridable while truth and rights remain fixed.
